implementation file: every validation guard in init (multilogperiod, errorlogname collision,
the multilog/batchmode/replayperiod domain checks) ran AFTER .z.m.schemas was already written,
so a THROWN init still left initialised[] reporting true. a caller who fixed their config and
retried was then silently treated as a RE-init, skipping first-time state seeding entirely -
the corrected retry itself threw on undefined .z.m.scheduled, and upd afterward threw on
undefined .z.m.logtabs. test.csv cannot catch this - scenario A's own init already succeeded
there

getmeta[`open] restart-recovery regression - a REAL bug found during a holistic re-read: a process
that dies before closing its currently-open period (a crash, or any exit skipping .z.exit) leaves
that row permanently null-end in the persisted stpmeta. getmeta[`open] used to APPEND a fresh row
on top with no check for one already there - confirmed directly by chaining three restarts
against the same log directory without a clean close: the metatable ended up with FIVE rows all
pointing at the exact same physical logfile, and subdetails' logfilelist (via getlogs`day`)
reported that one file five times over - a subscriber replaying "the day" would replay the same
data five times. fixed by reconciling against any existing null-end row for the same tables
before appending: same logname (a restart within the same period window) means RESUME it, not
duplicate it - a real crash (exit 1, skipping .z.exit) followed by a real restart into the same dir
run the crash/resume scenario - a real crash (exit 1) followed by a real restart into the same log directory
exactly one metatable row exists for the resumed table after restart - not duplicated on top of the crashed process's dangling row
the restart logged that it was resuming an existing logfile after an unclean prior shutdown
getmeta[`open] restart-recovery regression, other half: a stale null-end row with a DIFFERENT
logname than the one currently in use - a genuinely orphaned segment left by a process that
crashed, then was restarted only after enough real time passed to cross a period boundary.
reproducing that with a real elapsed-time gap would need an actual wait through a period
boundary, so this drives getmeta directly (white-box, the same technique daytimestampscenario/
custommodescenario already use) - seeding one fake stale row with a non-matching logname and
re-invoking getmeta[`open] to prove it is force-closed (msgcount left null, not guessed - a real

shared-handle regression - a REAL bug found during smoke testing: singular/periodic modes have
multiple tables sharing one logical log file, but openlog's reuse check used to be keyed on
(tbl;logname) - a second table resolving to the same logname as an already-open first table got
its own independent hopen call to that same path, producing a file di.tplog could not replay at
all ('rank, confirmed directly against the raw file before the fix). fixed by reusing ANY currlog
row with a matching logname, not just this table's own. this writes real alternating
trade/quote traffic through periodic mode and proves the file replays cleanly with the full row
count - not just that init/upd did not throw, which the corrupt-file version also satisfied

day-roll timestamp regression - a REAL bug found during smoke testing: dayrollover computed the
new day's currperiod (and next-roll target) from .z.p (real wall-clock "now") rather than the
EVENT time (data`p, the timestamp checkends actually detected the roll at). under any latency
between the two, the new log file landed in the correct new-day DIRECTORY but carried the WRONG
(stale) timestamp in its own FILENAME. fixed by using data`p throughout dayrollover.

child process here never calls subdetails - zero subscribers - so publish behaves the way a
